lesson.small: A friend asks what you would do with an unexpected free afternoon. Give a truthful answer and one detail. Ask a question back.
lesson.scenario: A friend invites you to a fictional weekend picnic. Explain what you did yesterday, what you are doing now and what you plan to do tomorrow. Ask about the time and location. After your first answer, the friend changes the meeting time. Respond with a simple sentence and a question.
lesson.writing: Write four sentences about a routine, yesterday, now and tomorrow. Turn two into negatives and two into questions.
lesson.note: Day 27 sentence production curriculum; everyday scenario.
lesson.noticing: I'm planning to visit the park. I haven't decided yet what time to leave. Let's narrow it down to two times. Is there any chance I could arrive later? I'll play it by ear. Yesterday I changed my mind about the route.
lesson.story: Describe a change of plans using two target chunks and three different tenses.
lesson.recovery: If you forget a word, describe it in simple English and finish the sentence.
soloQuestions: What will you do tomorrow if the meeting time changes?
lesson.writingCheck: I walk every day. I walked yesterday. I am walking now. I will walk tomorrow. I did not walk yesterday. Will you walk tomorrow?

ambiguity.sentence: The picnic is still on despite the cloudy weather.
ambiguity.context_clue: Despite the cloudy weather signals that the plan has not changed.

focus_drill: I'm planning to visit the park tomorrow.
